39c9d2c7fa.q: How do property managers in regional towns like Sale, Victoria manage professional boundaries when running into clients outside business hours?
39c9d2c7fa.a: Emma finds that in Sale, when encountering clients out of hours at locations like Woolworths, she appreciates that people generally respect that she is out of hours and rarely use the opportunity to raise issues. If someone does need advice requiring follow-up, she diverts them to contact her by email or phone during business hours. She notes that the small-town dynamic works both ways: while it makes her accessible, it also means that if someone is not answering their phone, locals often know where they work or can bump into them if needed.

218585b8c4.q: Why do evicted tenants typically not remain in small regional towns like Sale after eviction?
218585b8c4.a: Emma explains that in eviction situations, renters typically either leave town or go into hiding because they often owe money to multiple parties and not just the property manager. She notes that if they were to show their face, it would give the property manager an opportunity to follow up on the outstanding debt. More often than not, they are never seen or heard again in the small town, even months or years later when they may reappear on rental applications without listing the property they were evicted from.
